Processing status and dependencies

GET /api/status?include=processing collects domain-owned job reports. The status collector contains no workflow prerequisites or job-specific counting queries. Each ProcessingJob owns its report, declared dependency edges, and prerequisite evaluation. Execution and reporting call the same evaluation. Shared import barriers live with their job consumers in ImportPrerequisites, rather than in status collection.

On this page
  • Live reports
  • Execution and scheduling
  • Dependency metadata and GUI

Live reports

Existing outcome counts and percentages remain available. Additional fields provide the server-selected state, work.ready, work.waiting, work.retrying, blockedBy, nextRunAt, nextRetryAt, unit, and progressKnown. Ready includes eligible items currently executing; it is not a count of worker threads. The three work counts partition pending work. Source limitations and attention counts remain separate from execution state.

The shared policy chooses Running while a batch executes; otherwise Queued when any work is ready, Retrying when any work is deferred for retry, Waiting when any work awaits prerequisites, and Complete when no work remains. An active whole-job gate also reports Waiting before upstream discovery has established any pending count. Unknown totals use progressKnown=false.

Blockers identify an index, job, lock, or user action, with whole-job or item scope and Automatic or User-action resolution. Lock blockers report the current owner. Classification awaiting duplicate checks and energy awaiting classification are ordinary waits. A completed classification with no activity requires user action. Exploration applies its gate to the entire pending count without querying point eligibility for every pending track. Media duplicate changes are retriggers, rather than a whole-job blocking prerequisite.

A request memoizes shared import facts. Existing database aggregates gain filtered counts where possible. Current gates are evaluated on every poll; last batch results are not used as a stale prerequisite cache.

Execution and scheduling

BackgroundJobRunner distinguishes ownership of a continuation chain from execution. A domain batch signals its start after gates and work selection; execution is cleared in a finally block. Heavy batches obtain the shared resource lock before entering this execution scope. Typed batch outcomes preserve blockers or retry times while controlling continuation scheduling.

nextRunAt describes a scheduled check or an immediate continuation. It is registered at application startup and is not a promised start time. An occupied resource lock or scheduler can delay execution. Runtime markers remain in memory; work and retry deadlines remain in the database. Counts and markers can cross a commit boundary, so an executing batch may briefly have zero pending items.

Dependency metadata and GUI

Each enabled provider advertises Gate, Input, or Retrigger edges. The collector returns them once at the top level of Processing, with an opaque dependenciesVersion. A caller can pass that version in later requests; unchanged edges are omitted while live reports are still returned. The client keeps the cached graph and replaces it when its version changes.

The GUI displays server-selected states with distinct icons, visible blocker reasons, linked rows, and a compact dependency section inside each job's Details. Attention is an independent badge. Servers without the added state fields retain the previous client presentation. Indexer rows and map/routing services keep their existing state contracts.

Task counts play confirmed samples eight seconds behind the shared status clock, with a local render tick every 400 ms. Each row uses one completed count to keep its summary, pending count, ready work, details, and meter in step. Stable totals and outcomes allow playback; changed totals, outcomes, blockers, execution state, or decreasing completed counts reset it immediately. Finished work also settles immediately. Reduced motion shows the latest sample; hidden views pause their render tick, and reopening reuses the shared timeline. Polling remains unchanged.

Synthetic Google Health advertises its import, duplicate detection, activity classification, and energy gates through its own provider. It appears under Imports & sync, reports preparation before day totals are known, publishes committed day progress, and reports automatic retry times.
